aboutMore: Some numbers, since people ask. OurSpace runs on one laptop with a stick of RAM I installed myself, with a screwdriver, on a Sunday, and I am still proud of it. I read every wall post. All of them. It takes about three hours a night and it is the best three hours of my day. If you ever wonder whether anybody notices you here: I do. I noticed you before you noticed the site. Also my mom says hi. She doesn't know who you are. She says hi to the laptop, too.

blog.title: The Weekend I Built This Place
blog.body: People ask why I built OurSpace in a weekend. The honest answer is that I'd been on a message board for four years, a little one, maybe forty regulars. A guy in Ohio posted the weather every morning. A woman in Perth mailed us all recipes. In March the guy who ran it got a new job and switched it off. No warning. Just a page that said 'domain expired.' I didn't have anybody's email. I had forty usernames and nowhere to put them. So that weekend I wrote this site on a laptop, and the first thing I built was the friends list, so nobody could ever get lost again. That's why everybody starts with me as a friend. It isn't a feature. It's a promise. I hope the guy in Ohio is okay. If you're out there, buddy, it's still raining here too.

blog.title: A Field Guide to the Sounds the Laptop Makes
blog.body: Because people ask what 'the server is making a noise' means, here is the guide. STEADY HUM: all good, go back to sleep. HUM WITH A LITTLE RATTLE: dust, I'll blow it out Saturday. CLICK... CLICK... CLICK: that's the hard drive, and we do not discuss it, we back up. HIGH WHINE: the fan is asking for help, so I put a paperback under the back corner so it can breathe. SILENCE: this is the one. If it is ever silent the site is down and I'm already out of bed. I sleep with my head about eleven inches from it. People say that sounds lonely. It isn't, really. It's like sleeping next to a dog who does everything for everybody and never asks for anything. (Don't tell it I said that. It'll want a raise.)

blog.title: The Night the Site Went Down (And What Happened Next)
blog.body: At 10:41 PM last Thursday OurSpace went down. It was a power strip. It was always going to be a power strip. I was under my bed with a flashlight for two hours. When I came back up there were 63 messages and not one of them was angry. Brittany had posted a bulletin that said 'if anyone sees todd tell him it's ok.' Patrick had written 'are you ok' eleven times (he didn't know I couldn't read them yet). Somebody drew a power strip with a face. Chad wrote GREAT HUSTLE TODD. Vinyl_witch lit a candle. Even Marcus offered to 'take over temporarily,' which is a no, but a kind no. I sat on the floor with the laptop in my lap and read all of it. I do IT support for a living and nobody has ever sent me a bulletin. Anyway. The power strip is labeled now. The label says DO NOT.

blog.title: Backups: A Love Letter
blog.body: Every Sunday at 9 PM I burn a copy of OurSpace onto CD-Rs. Fifteen discs now, labeled by week in Sharpie. They live in a shoebox in the hall closet next to my mom's Christmas ornaments, which I consider the fireproof-adjacent spot. Everybody is in there. Patrick's page, with the picture of a rock. Darkangel's poems, all of them, even the one she says she deleted. Herp's whole profile (it's tiny, the most efficient file I own). Banana's bulletin, which compresses badly because it's loud. If it all ever goes away I can put it back. I've tested the restore twice. Nobody has ever asked me to restore anything, which means either I'm doing a great job or nobody needs me. I choose the first one. I really do.

survey.title: SURVEY: Know Your Admin (I filled it out so you don't have to ask)
qa: Name:
Todd. Founder, admin, night shift, day shift.
Age:
34. Old enough to remember when a modem was a status symbol, young enough to still say 'modem.'
First computer:
A Packard Bell my mom bought at Sears. I took the case off the first day. We don't talk about it. It still boots.
Desktop wallpaper:
A photo of a server rack I will never own. I call it Gerald.
Current away message:
back in 20 mins (this has been up since March)
Number of windows open right now:
11. One is OurSpace. Ten are OurSpace.
Best snack for 2 AM maintenance:
Cheez-Its. Not the big box. The big box is for celebrations.
Dream vacation:
A data center tour in Virginia. My mom asked if there are beaches. There are no beaches. I'm still going.
Weezer: blue album or green album:
Yes.
Last thing that made you smile:
Herp's bulletin. I read it four times. I think I understood it.
Biggest fear:
The word 'domain,' when it's followed by 'expired.'
Who do you talk to most:
The laptop, honestly. And then all of you, one at a time, in the order you post.
One thing you want people to know:
You can always find me here. I mean that in a non-creepy, uptime kind of way.

dms: Hi malten! Quick maintenance note: I signed your guestbook to make sure it was working. It says 'Todd was here.' That was supposed to be a test entry. I forgot to delete it. I'm leaving it.

Small update from the Server Room: the laptop battery has swollen to roughly the size of a sandwich, so I took it out. We now run directly off the wall. If the power flickers, we all go home together. :)

My mom asked what OurSpace is. I said it's a place where people put up pictures and talk. She said, 'Oh, like the church directory.' I've been thinking about that for three days. It's basically right.
I read your 'Why do we create?' post again last night. I think I create because at 3 AM somebody has to leave a light on. Anyway. Good post. Thank you for writing it.

Angela mailed me a three-page letter asking for a hit counter on OurSpace. I'm building it this weekend. It is a very small program and I am more nervous about it than I have been about anything since the weekend I built the site.
Just a reminder to back up your profile. I'm not saying anything is going to happen. I'm saying I have fifteen CD-Rs and a Sharpie and I am READY.
Weekly stat: 4,100 profile views, and about 3,100 of them were people checking whether their top 8 changed. It didn't. Nobody wants to hear this but I find it very peaceful.
Do you ever refresh the page just to see if anybody posted? I've decided that's called 'being a host.' It's not loneliness. It's hospitality. I looked it up.
A quick note on the green album: it gets unfair treatment. 'Hash Pipe' is a genuinely good song. I'll be taking questions in the guestbook.
Question for you as a fellow site owner: when it's quiet and nobody has posted in ten minutes, do you also say 'good, everything's running' out loud, to nobody? Just curious. No reason.
repliesExtra: Thanks for letting me know! I've written it on a sticky note, which is where all the serious things live.
Got it. I'll look into it right after I finish looking into the other eleven things. You're on the list. It's a good list.
I read that twice. Mostly because I like getting messages. Don't tell the others.
Have you tried refreshing the page? I know. I'm sorry. It really does help.
That's a great point and I'd like to add it to the roadmap, which is a piece of paper on my mom's fridge.
I appreciate you telling me. Most people just tell the laptop.
Noted! In unrelated news the laptop is running a little warm, so if I take a minute to reply, that's why.
Everything is fine. (I say this to the laptop, too.)
Thank you. I'm saving this one in the folder. The folder is called 'Nice Things.' It's getting thick.
Message received. I'm going to go sit with this and a sleeve of Cheez-Its.
statusesExtra: Todd is checking on the laptop fan. It sounds happy. He will check again in four minutes, which he considers 'relaxed.'
Todd just backed up everybody. Disc #15. The shoebox is getting heavy and so is his heart. (Normal. It's a good heavy.)
Todd would like to thank the many people who asked if he was okay after the outage. He is. You're all very kind. He is going to go sit in the dark and reread it.
Todd is building a hit counter for Angela. It is the most nervous he has been since the weekend he built the site.
Todd is at RadioShack looking for a 3-prong cable he doesn't need. He likes the smell. He'll be a minute.
Todd has read every wall post tonight. 211 of them. He's smiling. Good site. Good people. Going to bed. (Not going to bed.)

marcus: Hi Marcus! Thank you for draft 5. I read all six pages. The references were very impressive (your aunt in particular). I want to be honest with you: admin is mostly sleeping next to a laptop. It might not be what you pictured. But I'd love to talk about 'Honorary Wall Monitor.' It comes with a badge. It's a .gif.

Marcus, about the double-post warnings you've been issuing: I appreciate the enthusiasm. Please know the people you've warned are thrilled to hear from you. I think they take it as attention. Good work, buddy.
angela: Angela! The hit counter is in. It's a one-pixel-tall GIF I made last night. I can't promise it works but it feels right. I also signed your guestbook, entry 215. I signed it twice. The second time was to check it worked.
Your webring is the nicest corner of the whole internet, I think. I added OurSpace to it. Does that make us neighbors? I'd like that. -Todd
lars: Hi Lars! Thanks for the Ubuntu CD. I put it in the laptop to see what would happen and then took it out because the laptop made a face. I kept the CD. It's on the shelf next to the Weezer. I treat it like a gift.
Lars, I appreciate the kernel advice. I'm not ready to compile anything on the machine that holds everyone's friends list. I'll wait until you've done it twice more. On purpose both times.
doug: Doug, I made a small change: your page loads as plain text first now, pictures last. It's called progressive rendering, and it's what you've been doing in your head all along. You were ahead of the whole industry.

Doug, I read your library blog three times. Computer 3, by the window. I think about you biking there every Saturday. If you ever need something printed, I'll mail it. I have stamps. I have so many stamps.

keywordsExtra.backup: I have fifteen CD-Rs in a shoebox in the hall closet and I think of them as a very quiet family. Yes, you're on one.
keywordsExtra.laptop: The laptop is fine. (It's warm. It's always warm. I put a book under it. It's fine.)
keywordsExtra.weezer: Blue album AND green album. I don't discriminate. I will, however, discuss 'Hash Pipe' for an hour.
keywordsExtra.guestbook: Your guestbook is the best thing on the internet and I'm not saying that because I signed it 'Todd was here.' Okay I am.
keywordsExtra.webring: Angela's webring is the only part of the internet that has ever asked me to join it. I said yes immediately. I have never been so happy to be a link.
